subject: Cooking
title: Instant Coffee: The Convenience Revolution
description: Learn Instant Coffee: The Convenience Revolution in one minute.

hook.text: 50% of all coffee consumed worldwide is instant. Purists hate it. But it won the global market.

buildup.text: Nescafé launched in 1938 after Brazil asked Nestlé to find uses for surplus coffee beans rotting in warehouses.

discovery.text: Spray-drying or freeze-drying brewed coffee creates soluble granules — just add hot water. Ready in 10 seconds.

twist.text: WWII soldiers received instant coffee in rations — creating lifelong habits that drove postwar global adoption.

climax.text: In the UK, Greece, and much of Asia, instant coffee outsells fresh-brewed — convenience trumps craft for most.

punchline.text: Instant coffee isn't good coffee. But it's coffee for everyone, everywhere.

quiz.question: Why was Nescafé instant coffee originally created?
options: Brazil needed a use for surplus beans rotting in warehouses

details.summary: Instant coffee was perfected by Nestlé in 1938 as Nescafé, using spray-drying to turn brewed coffee into soluble powder. It now accounts for over 50 percent of coffee consumption in many countries.
details.whyItMatters: Instant coffee democratized caffeine access globally. In countries without café culture or brewing equipment, instant coffee is simply coffee — the default rather than the compromise.
takeaways: Nestlé launched Nescafé in 1938 as a solution to Brazilian coffee surpluses
Instant coffee is over 50 percent of consumption in many countries
Freeze-drying preserves more flavor than spray-drying methods

faq.question: How is instant coffee made?
faq.answer: Coffee is brewed at industrial scale, then water is removed. Spray-drying blasts liquid coffee into a hot chamber where it instantly becomes powder. Freeze-drying freezes brewed coffee then sublimes the ice under vacuum, better preserving flavor compounds.

faq.question: Why does instant coffee taste different from brewed?
faq.answer: The drying process destroys many volatile aromatic compounds that define fresh coffee's flavor. Spray-drying loses more than freeze-drying. Instant coffee also starts from lower-quality robusta beans more often.
